headline: Indonesia's Quiet Victory Over Extreme Poverty
meta_description: In four decades, Indonesia reduced extreme poverty from 86% to under 4%, lifting 130 million people toward stability.
summary_short: Indonesia has dramatically reduced extreme poverty in recent decades, with fewer than 4% of the population now living on less than $3 per day.
body:
In 1984, extreme poverty defined daily life for 86% of Indonesians. By 2025, that figure had plummeted to less than 4%—a transformation that has reshaped millions of lives.

The scale of this shift becomes clear in the numbers: 140 million people have moved out of extreme poverty over the past four decades, leaving approximately 10 million still living below that threshold. This reduction happened steadily, without the international headlines that accompanied similar progress elsewhere.

The story matters not because it's surprising but because it's real. While Indonesia's achievement has often been overshadowed by comparisons to other nations' gains, the country's sustained effort demonstrates that broad-based poverty reduction is possible. The journey from 86% to under 4% represents generations lifted from survival into stability.
quick_facts: 86% of Indonesians lived in extreme poverty in 1984
Less than 4% live on under $3 daily as of 2025
140 million people escaped extreme poverty in four decades
Approximately 10 million Indonesians remain in extreme poverty today
